selection_reason: This paper analyzes distributed speculative decoding for LLM inference/serving across edge devices and cloud servers, directly within the survey's inference and serving scope. It compares synchronous and pipelined distributed speculative decoding with co-located speculative decoding and cloud autoregressive decoding, derives bounded latency conditions, and identifies multi-tenant server capacity as the strongest case for offloading draft compute. The paper's capacity result depends on cross-client overlap; its per-request analysis assumes fixed, contention-free service times. It is an analytical study supported by cited measurements from prior systems, not a new end-to-end experimental evaluation.
title: Speculation at a Distance: Where Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding Actually Pays Off
